target_customer: Software teams and open-source projects paying for GitHub Actions minutes who want faster, cheaper builds
problem: GitHub-hosted Actions runners were slow and relatively expensive for CI workloads, so teams waited on builds and overpaid.
business_model: Usage-based, per-minute pricing for managed CI runners

founders.name: Adam Shiervani
founders.background_notes: YC page: over a decade of startup experience, started as a frontend developer.

exit.reason: Per a competitor's summary of the company's February 2026 announcement, GitHub's own runners had closed the performance gap BuildJet was built to fill; customers were given about eight weeks to move back. The company's own post was not opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running a bare-metal gaming CPU cloud with isolated, ephemeral VMs and GitHub integration is real infrastructure work but a known pattern.

defensibility.rationale: Switching required only one line in a workflow, and the advantage was cheaper hardware, so customers could leave as easily as they arrived.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GitHub improved its hosted runners and the company's announced reason for shutting down was that the performance gap closed; a crowded set of runner vendors also emerged (Depot, Namespace, Ubicloud, WarpBuild, RunsOn).

market_need_then: Not separately sourced for 2023. The company's pitch rested on GitHub-hosted runners being slow and costly; later vendor comparison pages show many alternatives appearing for the same pain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct developer copy with benchmark comparisons on open-source projects

branding.brand_signature: One-line change to runs-on plus public benchmarks on well known repositories
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt listing exists; no other community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name was clear and descriptive, but no press on the brand itself or community around it was found.

outcome_analysis: BuildJet sold faster, cheaper GitHub Actions runners and entered YC in Winter 2023 with two founders, with funding of roughly 500K reported only by aggregators. Its site now says the product was shut down, with job processing ending around March 2026. The sourced reason is that GitHub narrowed the performance gap, leaving a product dependent on GitHub's platform with a one-line switching cost and many competing runner vendors.
notes: Directory status says Active but the company site shows a shutdown banner, so the record is shutdown. Shutdown date and reason come from competitor blogs; Feb 6 announcement date and March 31 2026 end date are each from limited sources. Funding of about 500K (convertible note or pre-seed, dates conflict between Jan, Mar and Apr 2023) is only on aggregators and is not recorded as a round. Revenue of 330K by Sep 2025 is a single unverified source. Location conflicts across sources (Berlin, Tallinn). Competitor search found no coverage dated near early 2023, so the list is empty. Update: one round of about 500K is now recorded from CB Insights (convertible note, Y Combinator named), resting on a single database; VCBacked and FundedIQ call it a pre-seed in April 2023 and CB Insights dates it January 2023, so the date is given as 2023. Seedtable reports a total of $1M over 2 rounds but itemizes only the 500K, so a gap of about 500K is unexplained and not recorded.
